title: I built a horde-survival roguelite almost entirely with AI tools. Free demo, and what worked and what didn't
author: Plastic_Bag6171
selftext:
Darkfall is a pixel-art survivors-like where you play the villain: a dark sorcerer taking a bright kingdom piece by piece. The demo is out today, free, for Windows and macOS. I want to share how it was made, because the process surprised me more than the result.
    
    Code. The whole game is Godot 4 and GDScript, written by a coding agent (Claude Code). I describe what I want, play the build, and come back with complaints. The thing that made this work was giving the agent a way to run the game itself: a small editor plugin lets it start a scene, press keys, read values and take screenshots. Before that it would tell me a fix worked when it hadn't. After that it could check.
    
    Art. Characters, tilesets and icons come from PixelLab. What worked: generating one character, then using it as a style reference for big batches (25 to 64 sprites in one call), which kept everything in the same hand. What didn't: idle animations distorted the face, so idle is a single still frame. Some sprites came out with a one-pixel white rim that had to be cleaned by hand. And my first ground tileset was far too bright until I forced a fixed 13-colour palette.
    
    Music and sound. Stable Audio for music, ElevenLabs for effects. The first stage themes came out pleasant and completely wrong: asking for "a forest theme" gives you walking-around music. Asking for a fast battle theme first and the melody second fixed it.
    
    Balance. This is where AI helped least by guessing and most by measuring. Instead of asking "is this too easy", I had it script a maxed-out build, stand in a flood of enemies and count kills per second, then set enemy health from the numbers.
    
    What I still do by hand: every decision about what feels good. The agent is fast and wrong about fun in about equal measure.
    
    Demo: https://adirz.itch.io/darkfall
    Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NbZMZBboLBs
    
    Happy to answer anything about the workflow. I'd also love to hear where you stopped playing.
